evidence.text: BLS PPI shows the input-output spread narrowing again in IIIN's fiscal Q4 (Jul-Sep 2026 against Apr-Jun). Hot-rolled steel bars, plates and structural shapes (WPU101704, the closest public series to wire rod) averaged 313.9 against 297.7 (+5.4%). Steel wire (WPU101705) averaged 388.0 against 384.3 (+1.0%), and steel wire drawing industry output (PCU331222331222) 323.6 against 321.7 (+0.6%). Consensus EPS of $0.49 sits above Q3's $0.46, which implies flat-to-better margins after Q3 gross margin fell to 10.2% from 17.1% on 'inflation across nearly all cost areas' that outran pricing. September output prices did tick up (wire 391.1, drawing 325.3), consistent with price increases landing late in the quarter, which mainly helps Q1 FY27 commentary.
evidence.source: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/WPU101705 (steel wire). Same API for WPU101704, title at https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/WPU101704, and for PCU331222331222.

evidence.why_not_priced: A two-analyst EPS bar that has not moved in 90 days and sits above Q3 has not marked inputs to the Jul-Sep steel series. If the market had priced continued compression, the consensus would sit below $0.46 and the stock would have fallen into the print rather than rising 3.5% over 20 days. Part of it may be in the -20% from the 52-week high.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. The company has not confirmed Q4 rod costs. The direction matches management's own Q3 statement that wire rod, freight and other costs rose faster than prices (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764401/000143774926023670/ex_988377.htm), but the PPI understated IIIN's own Q3 pricing gap (IIIN ASP +2.3% q/q against drawing PPI +4.8%), so the mapping is loose. Weighted-average inventory costing on a $167M inventory (built $29M in nine months) lags and smooths rod cost changes. That cuts both ways: an earlier pre-buy at lower cost would cushion Q4.

evidence.text: Fiscal Q4 2026 is a 14-week quarter. The 10-K says 'Our fiscal year is the 52 or 53 weeks ending on the Saturday closest to September 30', and the Saturday closest to Wednesday 30 Sep 2026 is 3 Oct 2026. FY2023-FY2025 were all 52-week years. The extra week alone adds about 7.7% to shipments. The revenue consensus of $201.3M is only 1.8% above Q3's 13-week $197.7M and about 13.5% over the year-ago $177.4M, against ASP running about +8% y/y. That leaves room for a revenue beat of roughly 2-6% if per-week volume held, though the extra week also carries a week of fixed cost.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior 53-week quarter in the 7-print baseline. Revenue-led beats without margin have been bought little: Q3 FY26 grew revenue +9.9% y/y with a near-in-line EPS and moved +1.28%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is unclear whether either of the two analysts included the 14th week. A revenue consensus barely above a seasonally strong 13-week Q3 suggests at most part of it. If it were fully in, consensus revenue would be around $210M+, not $201M. The year-ago comparison is 13 weeks, so y/y growth will flatter the headline.
evidence.independence: The Q3 release data (shipments +11.9% sequential, ASP +8.0% y/y) supports the per-week run-rate arithmetic: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764401/000143774926023670/ex_988377.htm. There is no independent confirmation of Q4 volume, and the release noted data-center project delays.

evidence.text: The Upper Sandusky, Ohio welded-wire closure (8-K item 2.05, 2026-08-21) carries about $4.6M of restructuring: $1.0M non-cash impairment, $0.4M severance, $2.5M equipment relocation and $0.7M other. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: IIIN discloses the EPS impact of restructuring every time (Q3 FY25: $0.9M, $0.03 a share). No print in the baseline turned on a restructuring line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Headline GAAP EPS against a stale two-analyst bar could read as a miss in screens. Because the company quantifies the charge, most of this should be looked through, which is why it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Same 8-K as the following finding (the savings side of the same closure). They are counted once each in opposite directions because they land on different lines: this one on the reported quarter's one-off charge, the next on the forward cost base.

evidence.text: The same closure moves Upper Sandusky volume into plants with 'ample open capacity', with up to 65 positions cut and operations ending by end-October 2026. evidence.text: Q3 jet fuel ran above Southwest's assumption, and Southwest is unhedged. United's Q3 average was $3.90/gal (+60% yoy). Delta's GAAP fuel was $3.80/gal, and Delta said it absorbed more than $500M of fuel above its early-July guidance. Southwest guided Q3 at $3.70-3.75/gal on the July 17 curve and burned 564M gallons in Q2. An overage of about $0.15-0.20/gal is $85-113M pre-tax, or about $0.13-0.17 of adjusted EPS on 493M diluted shares. That would put Q3 adjusted EPS near or below the low end of the $0.50-0.75 guide unless RASM beats the +17.5-19.5% guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 Southwest's fuel came in below assumption ($3.92 vs $4.10-4.15) and the FY guide was still cut; the stock fell 6.19% on 2026-07-22. LUV has fallen on 5 of its last 7 prints (baseline).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Fuel is public, and analysts mark EPS to the curve, which is part of why LUV fell from 41.66 (10-09) to 38.80 (10-19). But the company has not updated its Q3 fuel assumption since July 22: there has been no 7.01 investor-update 8-K since then (EDGAR list). If the market had fully priced the overage, the 10-20/10-21 sector bounce would have left LUV lagging, and it did not (+4.2% off the low).

evidence.text: United's investor update puts Q4 2026 fuel at about $4.80/gal on the October 16 Gulf Coast curve. It also states that consensus assumes about $4.35/gal, $0.45 below its own assumption. The FY2026 adjusted EPS guide of $3.25-4.25 was set on the July 17 curve, so a cut or a low Q4 guide is likely, and the street may be marked to a stale fuel assumption as United says its own consensus is.
